newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Sinar Mas says Amcol deal being discussed.
newsitem.headline: Sinar Mas says Amcol deal being discussed.

text.p: Indonesian conglomerate Sinar Mas is considering injecting some assets into troubled Singapore property and trading company Amcol Holdings but is yet to come to a firm decision, Bisnis Indonesia reported on Tuesday.

The daily quoted Sinar Mas president director Eka Tjipta Widjaja as confirming the group would come to the rescue of Amcol, which has serious cash flow problems, but he added negotiations on how it would be done were still on.
"We have not decided yet how the injection of fixed assets would be done and what subsidiaries of Sinar Mas would be involved," Widjaja was quoted as saying.
Singapore's Business Times has reported that Sinar Mas would include some of its Indonesian palm plantations and a noodle plant in China as part of a $2 billion injection into Amcol Holdings.
Amcol was placed under interim judicial management in July after a Price Waterhouse report said the company had serious cash flow problems and had difficulty meeting its financial obligations.
In August, the judicial managers announced an agreement with the Sinar Mas group to rescue Amcol through the creation of a new company which would then take over the Singapore firm.
